Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

anywhere adverb

no matter where

also anywhere you like, anywhere at all, anywhere in the world, no matter where

classical

Cic. Fam. 6.1.1: nēmō sit quīn ubivīs quam ibi ubi est esse mālit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 14.22.2: ubivīs tūtius quam in senātū (Lewis & Short)

ubivīs

adverb

anywhere you like, anywhere at all

“Where you will”, of place where; ubivīs gentium, anywhere in the world (Ter. Hec. 3.1.4). Lewis & Short also gives “everywhere”. For “anywhere” after a negative or in a question, see somewhere.

Other words

  • quōvīs — anywhere (to any place)

    adverb of motion · also used · classical · Ter. Haut. 5.1.55: immō abeat quōvīs gentium (Lewis & Short); Plaut. Most. 4.2.7 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    Of going: “anywhere you like”. Lewis & Short marks it poetic; its passages are from comedy.

  • ubicumque — wherever; anywhere at all

    adverb and conjunction · also used · classical · Quint. 10.7.28: quidquid loquēmur ubicumque

    As a conjunction, “wherever”; standing alone, “anywhere at all, wherever it may be”.

  • ubilibet — anywhere, in any place

    adverb · also used · classical · Sen. Tranq. 1.6: ubilibet nōn dēfutūrus (Lewis & Short)

    Post-Augustan (Seneca); ubivīs is the usual word.

Examples

  • nēmō sit quīn ubivīs quam ibi ubi est esse mālit

    there is nobody who would not rather be anywhere than where he isCic. Fam. 6.1.1 (Lewis & Short)

  • immō abeat quōvīs gentium

    no, let him go anywhere in the worldTer. Haut. 5.1.55 (Lewis & Short)

  • nūllum nostrum usquam neglegentem esse sermōnem; quidquid loquēmur ubicumque, sit prō suā scīlicet portiōne perfectum

    none of our talk should ever be careless; whatever we say, anywhere, should be perfect in its own measureQuint. 10.7.28

  • cibus parābilis facilisque, ubilibet nōn dēfutūrus

    food that is cheap and easy, that will not be lacking anywhereSen. Tranq. 1.6 (Lewis & Short)

See also somewhere, everywhere, anyone, anything.

SourcesLewis & Short: ubivis · Lewis & Short: quovis · Lewis & Short: ubicumque · Lewis & Short: ubilibet

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
